title: The Clockmaker's Attic
revision_notes: Rev 1.0 initial design (2026-07-18). Adopts Level 1 rev-1.3 conventions as baseline: clue-gating with no-tell rule, uses-driven item lifecycle (declare every use; retain until all uses satisfied), non-collectible decoys (R6-003), requirement-flag state model (never step order), per-element overlay state rendering, container reveal/collect states, armed-item use, manual pickups.
theme: A tower clockmaker's attic workshop above the town. Every clock in the room stopped at the same moment. The attic backs directly onto the tower's great dial; the whole room is one connected machine of linkage rods, gears and chimes that the clockmaker left mid-thought. A gray cat still lives here.
framing_line: All his clocks stopped at six.
time_of_day: Late golden afternoon. Low warm sun through the dormer window (required: the cat's sunbeam patch, p02 staging); the great dial in z3 glows amber with transmitted daylight (required: mirrored-numeral legibility, p09).

win_condition.description: The attic's only exit, the stair door, is barred by a vault-style TIME LOCK connected by visible linkage rods to the tower movement behind the wall. Restore the great clock -- oil and wind it, set its hands to the release time shown on the clockmaker's 'will return' tag (set from BEHIND the mirrored dial), and start the pendulum. The strike train fires, the linkage lifts the door bar, and the player leaves down the stairs with the cat.

clue_gating.policy_revision: inherits L1 rev-1.3 policy verbatim (viewed_definition, persistence, no_tell_rule, D6/D7 semantics)
clue_gating.purpose: Protect code-like entries and sweep-brute-force surfaces from lucky/spoiler shortcuts while never false-blocking an earned solve. Gates reference only clues that carry the code's actual information.
clue_gating.viewed_definition: A clue counts as VIEWED the moment its designated close-up view has been displayed at least once. No dwell time, no comprehension check, no timers. Multi-instance clues count when ANY instance is displayed.
clue_gating.no_tell_rule: Gated attempts replay the puzzle's EXISTING failure grammar, presentation-identical to a wrong attempt. No distinguishing tell of any kind.
clue_gating.ungated_rationale_class: Free pickups, tool-on-hotspot oiling, tile seating with pop-back, the cat beat, mechanism completions (winding, pendulum push), and the gear train (a mechanically TRUE configuration must work when built -- gating physical truth reads as a broken machine) are physical acts, not code entries.
clue_gating.art_impact: None. Gated failures reuse existing failure states (cache boards/bricks simply don't budge -- identical to every inert board/brick; vault wheels spin without the hatch releasing; hand-setting simply doesn't trigger the strike).

elements: long workbench with clock parts (ambient, none collectible)
heavy flat-blade screwdriver in a bench rack (takeable)

chalk slate propped on the bench: wordless two-stage gear-train diagram -- crank circle ringed by 24 tally marks, small pinion marked XII, unknown wheel '?', coaxial small pinion marked VIII, unknown wheel '?', cam circle with a single notch and a door pictogram
small iron stove; numeral tile II lying on the cold hob
clockmaker's coat on a peg: pocket watch A in one pocket, numeral tile IIII in the other
wheel barometer on the wall (red herring rh-barometer: clock-like dial, fixed needle, sun/cloud/rain pictograms engraved -- inspect-only)
tall master longcase clock, case engraved with a small star (★), STOPPED at exactly 6:00 (hour hand on VI, minute hand on XII); its dial uses IIII for four

workroom door painted with a large hand-less clock dial: 12 tile sockets, 8 numeral tiles still seated (I, III, V, VI, VIII, IX, X, XII -- note seated IX shows the subtractive style), 4 sockets empty at the 2, 4, 7 and 11 positions
wooden tray fixed below the door dial holding one loose tile: IV (decoy; NON-COLLECTIBLE, lives in the tray -- R6-003)
packing crate of straw; numeral tile VII half-buried in the straw
linkage rods running along the ceiling from the direction of the stair door, vanishing into the workroom wall (foreshadows z3)
stair door (only exit) barred by a heavy horizontal bolt-bar seated in a vault-style time-lock housing; the bar connects to the ceiling linkage rods -- visibly a REMOTE mechanism, no keyhole
gray cat asleep on a cushion on a low bench in the dormer sunbeam (the cushion visibly has something flat beneath it)
dormer window over the town roofs, golden light
numeral tile XI on the dormer windowsill
small carved house symbol (⌂) on the beam beside the dormer, ringed by an engraved 12-notch circle (a clock-position ring)
floorboards below and around the dormer, uniform, none visibly special (cache board has NO independent tell -- the gate carries the info)

unlock.gate_description: Workroom door in z1 v-master, faced with the 12-socket painted clock dial; completing the dial with the correct numeral tiles trips its latch.

elements: floor-to-ceiling automaton wall: a carved town-scene mural with jointed figures, driven by an exposed two-stage gear frame -- fold-out hand crank at left carrying a fixed pinion stamped XII (12 teeth), empty square-arbor POST A (carries a fixed coaxial pinion stamped VIII, 8 teeth), empty square-arbor POST B driving the cam that runs the mural and, at cycle-end, a wall panel latch
the frame's main arbor is visibly SEIZED: rust bloom at the bearing, crank rocks a few degrees and stops

gear rack bolted to the wall holding six loose-mounted brass gears, each with countable teeth and a stamped Arabic count: 16, 24, 36, 40, 48, 72 (rack gears mount/return freely within the apparatus, NEVER enter inventory; the 48 invites a 48x48 idea -- there is only one 48: red herring rh-48-gear)
chimney breast passing through the room; one brick bears a small carved gear symbol (⚙) ringed by an engraved 12-notch circle; surrounding bricks uniform (cache brick has NO independent tell)

row of four dead wall clocks, ALL HANDS REMOVED, each with an engraved brass landmark plate beneath and a stamped offset: [1] Eiffel Tower plate stamped '+I', [2] Big Ben plate stamped '★' (no offset -- the reference; same star as the master longcase), [3] Mount Fuji plate stamped '+IX', [4] Statue of Liberty plate stamped '−V'; all four faces use IIII for four
small parts cabinet; top drawer holds a tin wind-up toy mouse with a butterfly key (takeable)

glass-front display case of assorted spare clock HANDS, case visibly screwed shut and painted over (red herring rh-hands-case: inspect-only; the world clocks never need hands -- the stamped offsets make the row purely informational)

unlock.gate_description: When the automaton mural completes one full correct cycle, a counterweight drops and a wall panel in z2 v-frame swings open onto the tower-clock chamber. Panel latches open permanently.

elements: the tower's great translucent dial seen FROM BEHIND, glowing amber with daylight; all numerals MIRROR-REVERSED (uses IIII); hand silhouettes visible through the glass
hand-setting crank on the motion works (moves the hands; 5-minute minute detents)
winding drum with a square key socket; drum bearing dry and squealing (needs oil before the key will turn)
long pendulum hanging dead still (can be pushed)
strike train and chime hammers, linked to the ceiling linkage rods that run off toward z1 (the door-bar linkage, seen end-to-end)

floor hatch in the platform: four brass combination wheels each engraved I-XII, headed left-to-right by pictogram plates: Big Ben ★, Eiffel Tower, Statue of Liberty, Mount Fuji (NOTE: different order than the z2 clock row -- binding is by pictogram, not position)

zones.name: The Clockmaker's Vault (under the dial platform)

unlock.gate_description: Floor hatch in z3 v-dial releases when the four wheels read VI-VII-I-III under their pictogram headers.

elements: small strongroom below the platform
large square-bit winding key on a hook (takeable)
brass 'will return' shop tag hanging on a nail: a miniature FRONT-VIEW clock dial with fixed hands at 7:20 above a small door pictogram (takeable clue item)
second cat cushion and an empty saucer (quiet lore; the cat's other nap spot)
shelf of ledgers and a wrapped unfinished pocket watch (ambient, inspect-only)

derived_conditions.name: timelock-release
derived_conditions.evaluation: Continuously evaluated boolean over three persistent states, TRUE the moment all three hold REGARDLESS of achievement order. On first TRUE it fires the strike beat and LATCHES state door-bar-raised permanently (later hand-fiddling cannot re-lock the door). This is a condition, never an event sequence.
inputs: state: hands-at-release (from p09-set-hands, continuously evaluated until the latch fires)

nodes.name: Heavy flat-blade screwdriver
nodes.notes: Multi-use tool; NEVER consumed; retained for the whole level (L1 poker lesson -- full uses list declared).

nodes.name: Pocket watch A (single-handed watchman's dial)
nodes.notes: Clue-carrier, inspectable anywhere: case back engraved with the house symbol ⌂; single hand STOPPED on III; its dial uses IIII (clu-face-convention instance).

nodes.name: Tin wind-up mouse
nodes.notes: Consumed BY DESIGN at p02 (the cat keeps it); it has no other uses, so consumption is soft-lock-safe. Wound-and-placed anywhere else: it skitters a small circle and RETURNS to inventory (developer_notes D4).

nodes.name: Pocket watch B (single-handed watchman's dial)
nodes.notes: Clue-carrier, inspectable anywhere: case back engraved with the gear symbol ⚙; single hand STOPPED on IX; dial uses IIII.

nodes.name: Great wheel (bronze gear, 64 teeth, stamped 64)
nodes.notes: Mountable/unmountable freely on either post; returns to inventory when unmounted. Never consumed.

nodes.name: Long-spout oil can
nodes.notes: Multi-use; NEVER consumed/emptied; retained until both uses satisfied and beyond.

nodes.name: 'Will return' tag (mini dial fixed at 7:20, door pictogram)
nodes.notes: Clue-carrier for p09; inspectable anywhere. Shows the FRONT view of a dial.

nodes.content: Wordless chalk schematic of the z2 gear frame: crank circle ringed with 24 tally marks; fixed pinion XII; unknown wheel '?'; fixed coaxial pinion VIII; unknown wheel '?'; cam circle with one notch and a door pictogram. Encodes: (A/12) x (B/8) = 24, i.e. A x B = 2304 -> 36 and 64.
House symbol ⌂ on case back; single hand frozen on III. Read at the ⌂ ring by the z1 dormer: 3-o'clock direction.
nodes.viewed_when: watch A inventory inspect close-up displayed

nodes.content: Gear symbol ⚙ on case back; single hand frozen on IX. Read at the ⚙ ring on the z2 chimney: 9-o'clock direction.
nodes.viewed_when: watch B inventory inspect close-up displayed

nodes.content: Carved ⌂ ringed by a 12-notch clock-position circle: the in-scene 'apply a clock direction HERE' anchor. 3-o'clock = toward the third floorboard right of the dormer.
nodes.viewed_when: dormer ring close-up displayed (not part of the gate; anchor only)

nodes.content: Carved ⚙ ringed by a 12-notch clock-position circle. 9-o'clock = the brick directly left of the ring.
nodes.viewed_when: chimney ring close-up displayed (not part of the gate; anchor only)

nodes.content: Master clock stopped at exactly 6:00; case bears the same ★ as the Big Ben plate and the vault's Big Ben wheel header. Establishes reference time = 6.

Four hand-less clocks with landmark plates and stamped offsets: Eiffel +I, Big Ben ★ (reference), Fuji +IX, Liberty −V. With reference 6: Eiffel 7, Big Ben 6, Fuji 6+9=15 -> III on a 12-hour dial, Liberty 6−5=1. Landmark identification is NOT required -- pictogram matching to the vault headers suffices.
Every clock face in the attic writes four as IIII (traditional dial convention), while nine stays IX. Instances: watch A dial, master longcase dial, all four world-clock faces.
nodes.viewed_when: ANY instance displayed (single shared flag; NOT a gate -- fairness evidence for the IIII tile choice)

nodes.content: The great dial's numerals read mirror-reversed from behind -- the standing evidence that the back view is a MIRROR of the front, so the return tag's front-view 7:20 must be set as its mirror image.
nodes.viewed_when: great dial close-up displayed (self-satisfying: the setting crank lives in this close-up)

nodes.content: Mini FRONT-VIEW dial fixed at 7:20 over a door pictogram: the time-lock's release time.

Visible linkage rods run from the stair door's time-lock bar along the ceiling into the wall, and re-emerge in z3 at the strike train: the door is opened BY the clock. Foreshadowing/orientation, not a gate.

Nudging the cat or offering ANY inventory item gets the same terminal refusal: one slow blink, the cat resettles heavier on the cushion; offered items return unspent. Categorical ('this will never work'), identical on repeat, no escalation. Petting is allowed (purr, no state change). The only thing that moves a cat is prey.

nodes.name: The numeral-dial door
nodes.mechanic: environmental scavenger (4 hidden tiles) + positional numeral seating + convention discrimination (IIII vs IV)
nodes.input: Seat numeral tiles into the four empty sockets (positions 2, 4, 7, 11).
nodes.derivation: Standard clock-face layout gives each numeral its position (the 8 seated tiles anchor it). The trap: the tray offers an IV tile and the seated IX shows the subtractive style, but every real dial in the attic writes four as IIII (clu-face-convention). Seating IV in socket-4: the mechanism whirs, stalls, and the IV pops back to its tray; seating IIII completes the dial and trips the latch.

clue_gate.rationale: Physical seating with pop-back rejection, self-anchored by the 8 seated tiles. The only knowledge fork (IIII vs IV) costs at most one extra attempt, and the convention evidence stands in three in-room faces -- gating would add friction for zero anti-spoiler gain.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong tile or wrong socket: whir-stall, tile pops back (inventory tiles to inventory, tray tile to tray). Unlimited attempts, correct seats persist.

nodes.name: The cat and the mouse
nodes.input: Wind the tin mouse (built-in butterfly key) and set it on the floor near the cat's bench.
nodes.derivation: The cat refuses everything else (clu-cat-refusal); the cushion visibly has something flat beneath it. The mouse skitters, the cat pounces and chases it to the stair-door corner, keeping it -- and settles there for the rest of the level (by the exit).
clues: flat shape under cushion visible in close-up

clue_gate.rationale: Physical/character beat with a single affordance; the refusal grammar already kills wrong theories categorically (L1 D4 lesson).

yields.via: cushion now liftable; watch B beneath

nodes.notes: Mouse is consumed by design (cat keeps it); it has no other uses. Placed anywhere but at the cat, it circles and returns to inventory (D4).

nodes.name: Dormer floorboard cache
nodes.location: z1 v-door, third floorboard right of the dormer ring
nodes.mechanic: clock-hand-as-pointer (angle applied at an engraved clock-position ring) + tool pry
nodes.input: Pry the board at the ⌂ ring's 3-o'clock direction with the screwdriver.
nodes.solution_fixed: board at 3-o'clock of the ⌂ ring (board index D3)
nodes.derivation: Watch A: ⌂ on the case back binds it to the dormer ring; its single hand on III reads as a direction on the ring's 12-notch circle -- 3 o'clock, toward the third board to the right.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Until watch A has been inspected, EVERY board (including the correct one) refuses to budge under the screwdriver -- presentation-identical to the always-inert boards. No tell. Stale case: none (prying is an explicit act, re-attempted after viewing).
clue_gate.rationale: The cache board has NO independent visual tell, so a sweep-pry of the dormer boards would brute-force the pointer puzzle (same class as L1's six-tap astrolabe risk). Watch A carries the cache's entire information; the gate cannot false-block an earned solve.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong board OR gated attempt: doesn't budge, identical. No damage, unlimited attempts.

nodes.name: Chimney brick cache
nodes.location: z2 v-frame, brick left of the ⚙ ring
nodes.mechanic: clock-hand-as-pointer + tool pry (second instance, cross-zone: watch found in z1 via the cat, applied in z2)
nodes.input: Pry the brick at the ⚙ ring's 9-o'clock direction with the screwdriver.
nodes.derivation: Watch B: ⚙ binds it to the chimney ring; hand on IX = 9 o'clock = directly left of the ring.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Identical grammar to p03: no brick budges until watch B has been inspected. No tell.
clue_gate.rationale: Same anti-sweep rationale as p03; watch B is the sole information carrier.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong brick OR gated attempt: doesn't budge, identical. Unlimited attempts.

nodes.name: Free the seized arbor
nodes.input: Use the oil can on the gear frame's rust-bloomed bearing.
clues: rust bloom at the bearing; crank visibly rocks a few degrees and stops

clue_gate.rationale: Tool-on-hotspot physical act; the seizure is self-evident. Nothing code-like to protect.

yields.state_semantics: Persistent latched flag; crank now turns freely (with whatever gears are mounted).

nodes.name: The automaton gear train
nodes.mechanic: gear-ratio reasoning (two-stage reduction; meshing train) -- LEVEL SIGNATURE MECHANIC
nodes.input: Mount one gear on POST A (meshing the crank's fixed 12-tooth pinion; POST A carries a fixed coaxial 8-tooth pinion) and one on POST B (meshed by that pinion, driving the cam). Then crank through one full cam revolution.

solution_fixed.arrangement: EITHER order -- 36 on A with 64 on B, or 64 on A with 36 on B (ratio product commutes; both are correct by design, multiple valid solves)

nodes.derivation: Slate: (A/12) x (B/8) = 24 -> A x B = 2304. Available: rack {16, 24, 36, 40, 48, 72} + the found 64-tooth great wheel. Unique pair anywhere in the level: 36 x 64 (the 36 is on the rack; the 64 must be found via p03 -- the great wheel is strictly required). The 48 tempts 48 x 48 = 2304 exactly, but only one 48 exists (rh-48-gear).
clues: stamped tooth counts (Arabic) + physically countable teeth on every loose gear
Roman XII / VIII stamps on the fixed pinions
live mechanical feedback: with ANY meshing pair mounted the crank turns and the cam/mural visibly runs at the resulting speed

clue_gate.rationale: Mechanical truth: a correctly built 24:1 train MUST work whether or not the slate was seen -- gating it would read as a broken machine. The brute-force surface (~30 ordered pairs, each needing a cranking test) is real but tedious, and the visible too-fast/too-slow cam feedback is INTENDED reasoning material, not a leak. Flagged in the summary as a difficulty judgment call.

yields.via: at exactly 24:1 the mural completes one full clean cycle (sun crosses the carved town, the watchman figure strikes his bell), a counterweight drops, and the wall panel swings open -- latches open permanently

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong ratio: the cam visibly runs too fast or too slow; at cycle-end the panel latch ratchets and SLIPS with a clack (identical clack for every wrong ratio -- speed itself is the only differential feedback, by design). Gears freely remountable; rack gears return to the rack, the great wheel returns to inventory if unmounted. No lockout.

nodes.name: The four-wheel vault hatch (NUMERIC-CODE LOCK -- standing user directive honored)
nodes.mechanic: numeric combination lock; time-zone offset reasoning with cross-zone clue binding
nodes.input: Set four wheels (each engraved I-XII) under pictogram headers: Big Ben ★, Eiffel, Liberty, Fuji.
nodes.derivation: Master clock (z1) stopped at 6:00 and shares the ★ with the Big Ben plate/header -> reference 6. z2 plates give offsets: Eiffel +1 -> 7; Liberty −5 -> 1; Fuji +9 -> 15 -> III on a 12-hour wheel. Header order at the vault differs from the z2 row order, forcing pictogram matching. Landmark-name knowledge is never required -- pictograms match pictograms; the offsets are stamped in-world.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Wheels spin freely at all times; while gated the hatch stays shut on ANY setting including the correct one -- presentation-identical to a wrong code. Wheels retain position. Stale-correct-wheels case resolves via D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry.
clue_gate.rationale: 12^4 = 20,736 combinations invites persistent fiddling and walkthrough spoilers; both gating clues carry the code's entire information and live in permanently reachable earlier zones (z1, z2), so no earned solve can be blocked.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong code OR gated attempt: hatch stays shut, identical. Wheels keep position; no lockout.

nodes.name: Oil and wind the movement
nodes.mechanic: mechanism completion (two-item: oil the dry drum bearing, then crank the winding key)
nodes.input: Oil can on the squealing drum bearing; winding key in the square socket; crank until the drive weight rises fully.
nodes.solution_fixed: itm-oilcan on drum bearing, then itm-winding-key in socket
clues: dry squeal + rust at the drum bearing; square socket visibly matches the key's square bit; drive weight visible on its line

clue_gate.rationale: Mechanism completion; both needs are self-evident (squeal, matching socket). Physical acts, not code entries.

yields.state_semantics: Persistent latched flag; drive weight fully raised. Feeds cond-timelock-release.

nodes.failure_behavior: Key before oil: key seats but won't turn, drum squeals -- oil need is restated diegetically. Nothing consumed.

nodes.name: Set the hands from behind (mirrored dial)
nodes.mechanic: clock-hands dial entry with a mirror-reversal inference -- clock hands as BOTH time and geometry
nodes.input: Turn the setting crank to position the great dial's hands (5-minute detents on the minute hand).
nodes.solution_fixed: mechanism (FRONT) time = 7:20; equivalently, the BACK view the player sees must show the mirror image of 7:20 (see developer_notes D1 for the rendering/state contract)
nodes.derivation: The return tag shows the release time 7:20 as a FRONT view. The player stands BEHIND the dial: numerals are visibly mirror-reversed (clu-mirrored-numerals), so naively copying the tag's hand positions onto the back view sets the front to 4:40 and nothing happens. The aha: mirror the tag. Any-order verification: the strike fires the moment all three release conditions hold.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Crank always turns and hands always move (a frozen crank would read broken); while gated, hands-at-release simply never asserts, so the condition cannot fire -- indistinguishable from having the wrong time set. clu-mirrored-numerals is self-satisfying (same close-up as the crank) and is deliberately NOT in the gate. Stale case: correct front-time set while gated, tag viewed later -- D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry (or on any subsequent state change) asserts the flag.
clue_gate.rationale: 144 detent combinations plus the tag being on the required path (z4 precedes any possible knowledge of 7:20) means the gate can never false-block; it closes the persistent-fiddling/spoiler path only.

yields.state_semantics: Continuously evaluated: TRUE while front-time = 7:20. Once cond-timelock-release latches, later hand movement is irrelevant (door bar stays raised).

nodes.failure_behavior: Any non-7:20 front time (including the un-mirrored 4:40 trap) OR gated state: nothing -- the clock simply sits at that time. No tell beyond absence of the strike. Unlimited adjustment.

nodes.name: Start the pendulum
clues: dead-still pendulum in an otherwise restorable machine

yields.state_semantics: Persistent latched flag (stylized: once pushed it keeps swinging -- weakly if unwound, fully once wound; the flag is order-free either way).

nodes.name: Open the stair door and leave
nodes.mechanic: endgame free action once the time lock releases
nodes.input: When cond-timelock-release latches: the strike train fires (chimes), the linkage rods articulate along the ceiling in BOTH z3 and z1, and the door bar lifts. Return to z1, open the door.
clues: the cat, relocated to the door since p02, stands and stretches when the bar lifts (silent nudge)

clue_gate.rationale: Endgame free action; nothing to gate.

yields.beat: the door swings onto the tower stairs in evening light; the cat trots out ahead of the player, tail up

solve_path_notes.structure: Spine: z1 tile scavenge -> p01 -> z2. Then THREE parallel workstreams that cross-bind zones: (1) pointer-watch stream: watch A (z1 coat) -> dormer cache -> great wheel; mouse (z2) -> cat (z1) -> watch B -> chimney cache (z2) -> oil can; (2) machine stream: oil arbor -> gear train -> z3; (3) knowledge stream: view master time (z1) + world-clock row (z2) -> vault code. In z3: vault -> z4 (key + tag) -> endgame trio (wind / set hands / pendulum) in ANY order -> strike -> z1 exit. Any interleaving satisfying the requirement edges is valid.
example_ordering_A: take coat items (watch A + tile IIII)
view master clock close-up (satisfies clu-master-time AND a clu-face-convention instance)
example_ordering_B_pendulum_first: view clu-slate-ratio AFTER experimenting at the frame (slate is confirmatory, not gating)
p08 (winding completes the trio -- condition latches here)
example_ordering_C_knowledge_first: view clu-master-time and note 6:00 before anything else
view clu-worldclock-row and pre-compute VI-VII-I-III long before the vault exists
inspect watches A and B in either order
p04 then p03 (cache order is free)
p07 first thing in z3 (gates already satisfied) -> z4
solve_path_notes.state_model: All progression is satisfied-requirement flags (zone unlocked, item held, state latched, clue viewed) plus one derived condition (cond-timelock-release, an order-free AND over three states -- orderings B and C exercise different completion orders). No step-order tracking anywhere. p06 accepts BOTH gear arrangements (unordered set).

developer_notes.note: Canonical clock state is FRONT time; solution_fixed is front 7:20. The z3 close-up RENDERS the back view: numerals and hand angles mirrored across the vertical axis (a front hour-angle of θ renders at −θ). The setting crank changes front time; the render stays consistently mirrored. Do NOT implement a second 'back time' variable. Art: mirrored numerals must be obviously reversed (IIII, VII especially legible-in-reverse) at close-up resolution -- this is the puzzle's entire evidence base.

Re-evaluate on every change to clock-wound, hands-at-release, or pendulum-running, plus on z3 close-up entry (D6 stale case for p09). On first TRUE: play strike beat (chimes + rod articulation in the current zone), latch door-bar-raised permanently. Never gate on achievement order.

L1 D4 lesson applied from day one: nudging the cat OR offering ANY inventory item produces the identical terminal refusal (one slow blink, resettles heavier); offered items return unspent; no escalation or variation across repeats. Petting: purr, no state change, always available. After p02 the cat sits by the stair door; same refusal grammar applies there.

Wound and placed anywhere except at the cat: skitters a small circle and returns to inventory automatically. At the cat: p02 fires, mouse leaves inventory permanently (cat keeps it -- it has no other uses; declared soft-lock-safe).

With any meshing pair mounted and the arbor freed, cranking runs the mural at the true resulting ratio -- visible speed IS intended feedback (mechanical truth, not a leak). Every wrong ratio ends its cam cycle with the SAME latch-slip clack; only speed differs. Gears mount/unmount freely; rack gears live in the apparatus (never inventory); the great wheel returns to inventory when unmounted. The fixed pinions (XII, VIII) are not removable.

Inherit L1 D6 verbatim: gated puzzles re-evaluate (gate AND solution) on every input/attempt event AND on entry into the puzzle's close-up. Stale cases here: p07 (wheels pre-set correctly while gated) and p09 (front 7:20 pre-set while gated). p03/p04 have none (pry is an explicit act).

Inherit L1 D7: one persistent saved boolean per gating clue (clu-watch-a, clu-watch-b, clu-master-time, clu-worldclock-row, clu-return-tag) plus the non-gating shared flag for clu-face-convention. Set on first display of any qualifying view; never cleared; ordinary satisfiable requirements.

The z1 stair door must never accept item use or code input: its housing has no keyhole (art requirement). Any interaction while barred: the bar rattles once against the linkage -- identical every time, pointing attention up the rods (the door teaches 'solve me elsewhere').

red_herrings.design: The subtractive IV tile sits ready in the tray under the door dial, and the dial's own seated IX validates the subtractive style. Every actual clock face in the attic uses IIII (three in-room instances). NON-COLLECTIBLE: lives in the tray, seats-and-pops-back (whir-stall) from socket-4. Fairness valve: worst case one extra attempt; the convention is flavor-turned-teaching, not a wall.

48 x 48 = 2304 exactly -- the arithmetic works, inviting a hunt for 'the second 48'. Only one exists, anywhere. NON-COLLECTIBLE (rack gears never enter inventory); mounting the lone 48 with anything else gives honest wrong-speed feedback. Time-cost trap only; the 36 x 64 solution uses parts the player demonstrably has.

red_herrings.node: z2 display case of spare clock hands
red_herrings.design: The hand-less world clocks scream 'find and refit the hands'. The spare-hands case is screwed shut and painted over (inspect-only, NON-COLLECTIBLE contents); the world clocks accept no interaction. The stamped offsets on the plates are the actual payload -- the row is informational, not restorable. Defusal: categorical inertness from first contact, L1 feed-cup lesson.

A clock-like brass dial that is not a clock: fixed needle, engraved sun/cloud/rain pictograms in close-up. Invites hand-setting/code theories; accepts no input. Pure time-cost; the pictograms make its non-clock nature legible without words.

anti_softlock_invariants: No consumable can be wasted: the toy mouse is the ONLY by-design consumed item and has exactly one use (p02); anywhere else it returns to inventory (D4).

clock-wound and pendulum-running are persistent latches; hands-at-release is continuously evaluated; cond-timelock-release latches door-bar-raised permanently on first TRUE -- later hand movement cannot re-lock the exit.
All locks/codes (p01, p03, p04, p06, p07, p09) have unlimited attempts, no lockouts; wheels and hands retain position; gears freely remountable.
Zones never re-lock (z2 door latch, z3 panel, z4 hatch all latch open permanently).

Every clue_gate references only clues in permanently reachable zones or inventory items on the required path (watches A/B, return tag are inspectable anywhere, forever); clue-viewed flags persist in the save (D7). So whenever a gated puzzle is reachable, its gate is satisfiable.
The cat cannot be harmed or blocked into an unwinnable state; it grants watch B exactly once; failed offers return items unspent (D3).

colorblind_safety: No puzzle uses color differentiation anywhere. Gears differ by SIZE + countable teeth + stamped numerals; tiles by engraved numerals; world clocks by landmark SILHOUETTES + stamped offsets; vault wheels by pictogram headers + engraved numerals.
Brass vs bronze vs steel finishes are ambient only, never load-bearing.
Mirrored-dial reading depends on numeral SHAPE reversal, not color.
Cat/mouse, oiling, winding: state changes are shape/motion (weight height, pendulum motion, bar position), never color.

designer_difficulty_estimate.escalation_rationale: vs L1's 6.0: (1) two genuine multi-step inference chains with light arithmetic -- gear-ratio product (A/12 x B/8 = 24) and time-zone offsets with a 12-hour wrap; (2) longer dependency chains (mouse -> cat -> watch B -> chimney cache -> oil -> arbor -> gear train -> zone 3); (3) heavier cross-zone clue binding (z1 master time + z2 plates -> z3 vault; z1 slate -> z2 frame; watches found in one zone, applied in another); (4) one perceptual inversion (mirrored dial) with a designed trap answer (4:40). Difficulty comes from chain depth and layered reasoning, never pixel-hunting: every cache is anchored by an engraved ring, every code's data is stamped in-scene.
